Hi Sarah 


Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap of what we covered and the next steps so we can move this forward with your security and procurement teams.

Recap (audit logging capabilities)
- Admin activity logs: user/admin console actions, role changes, permission grants/revokes.
- API request logs: request/response metadata, requester identity, endpoint, latency/error codes.
- Exportability: daily exports (JSON/JSONL or CSV) to customer S3 buckets, or live streaming to SIEM (syslog/CloudWatch).
- Immutability / append-only: logs written append-only with optional S3 Object Lock / retention policies; tamper-evidence via write-once configuration.
- Retention controls: configurable per-account retention windows; legal/archival exports available.
- Access & encryption: logs encrypted at rest and in transit; role-based access + audit trail for log access.

Questions we flagged for you: SOC 2 status and any regulated scope (GDPR/HIPAA) or specific retention/immutability requirements your security team has. Per our conversation, attached is a short SOC 2 summary and our vendor security questionnaire for your team to start filling out.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (one-page summary), redwood_vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx (fillable).

Appreciate the concise recap. A few quick follow-ups from our side so we can drive the questionnaire internally:

- Immutability: Can you confirm whether Redwood supports WORM-style locking (object lock with legal hold) and whether the customer can independently manage retention/lock periods for exports you send to our S3? We need chain-of-custody assurances.
- Export format: JSONL is preferred (we ingest into our analytics pipeline). Can you confirm streaming vs batch (both ok? limits?).
- Auditability: Do you provide a tamper-evident checksum or signing of exported bundles? Any guidance on proving integrity during audits?

I started the vendor questionnaire and attached our internal procurement checklist (we'll fill and return). Also cc'd procurement. Our DPO (dpo@acme.com) will want to review the SOC 2 summary.

Hi Sarah 


Thanks 


Thanks 


- WORM / immutability: Yes. We support S3 Object Lock on exports we deliver to customer buckets. Customers can configure retention/Legal Hold for their bucket objects; Redwood can also apply initial retention metadata on export but we recommend customer-managed locking for legal control. For internal platform logs we use append-only write patterns and a tamper-evident pipeline; for customer exports we provide MD5/SHA256 checksums and signed manifest files so you can validate integrity.

- Export formats & delivery: We can deliver exports as JSONL (recommended for high-volume request logs) or CSV. Delivery options: daily batch exports to your S3, ad-hoc on-demand exports, or streaming to your SIEM via syslog/CloudWatch events. Streaming does have rate limits; we'll provide a throughput guidance doc in the next 48 hours.

- Auditability: We provide signed manifests with SHA256 checksums and a timestamped manifest. For higher-assurance workflows we can provide an export signed with our platform key and provide a verification script.

Attachments: acme_sample_request_logs.jsonl (sample of anonymized request logs).
